candidate.name: benchmark release-population lineage certificate
candidate.domain: cooperative perception and collaborative autonomous driving benchmarks
candidate.question: Can the physical events, ego roles, and cohort population defined by a released dataset or evaluation index be mechanically regenerated from a public generator, pinned source commit, pinned container, and manifest, with training and evaluation blocked before execution when the regenerated population semantics differ from the released index?

independence.note: The audit tests functional equivalence directly. It does not preserve the candidate by treating generic provenance, metadata, leakage checks, or replay claims as exact equivalents, and it does not weaken a collision because the colliding work is outside cooperative perception.

conditions.name: canonical release population
conditions.requirement: The release artifact or index explicitly determines a canonical set of evaluation units containing physical-event identity, frame or time extent, ego identity and role, ordered or canonically sorted cooperating cohort membership, split, and every population-changing filter or loader option.

conditions.name: mechanical regeneration
conditions.requirement: A public generator can regenerate that canonical population from declared inputs using a pinned source commit, content-addressed container image, simulator and asset versions, configuration, random seeds, and deterministic or explicitly normalized population projection.

conditions.name: cryptographic binding
conditions.requirement: A signed or content-addressed certificate binds the release index, canonical population projection, generator commit, container digest, inputs, parameters, and resulting manifest rather than merely recording prose or file paths.

conditions.name: fail-closed preflight
conditions.requirement: Before any training or evaluation consumes samples, an executable verifier regenerates or validates the canonical population and halts on set inequality, role mismatch, cohort mismatch, split mismatch, omitted units, extra units, or unbound population-changing configuration.

canonicalProjection.comparison: Exact equality after documented canonicalization; aggregate counts, schema compatibility, file checksums, and approximate distribution similarity are insufficient.

nonEquivalentClasses: Byte or file lineage that proves which artifacts and commands were used but treats their semantic contents as opaque.
Schema, metadata, datasheet, data-card, or model-card systems that describe fields or intended use without regenerating and comparing the evaluation population.
Data-quality or data-contract checks that validate user-authored predicates but provide no standard cooperative-perception population projection or generator binding.
Leakage, contamination, duplication, corruption, or robustness audits that test overlap or perturbations rather than release-to-generator population identity.
A public simulator, replay tool, dataset builder, or generated index without a certificate and fail-closed semantic equality check.
A signed manifest or software-supply-chain attestation whose predicate covers only files, images, commands, or generic arbitrary metadata.

searchAudit.foundationalExceptions: Earlier datasheets, model cards, in-toto, and related specifications were checked because the request explicitly names these lineages or because later tools build on them.
searchAudit.queryMethod: Broad web discovery followed by primary-source verification against formal proceedings, publisher pages, standards documentation, official project documentation, and official source repositories.

sourceAttempts.outcome: Verified formal records for OPV2V, V2Xverse, RCP-Bench, Kubric, Croissant, DataComp, DataPerf, DataLad workflow provenance, RO-Crate workflow provenance, Data Cards, MedPerf, and representative contamination audits. No formal publication was found that implements all E1-E4.

Checked recent generator, task-metadata, benchmark-audit, and cooperative-perception work, including SimBEV2X and Croissant Tasks. Recent preprints narrowed the gap but did not expose an E1-E4 implementation.

Inspected official repositories and documented generator, replay, index, split, container, manifest, and verification paths. SimBEV2X was additionally inspected at commit d936d658e4e4075909ff9417805a8ead01d0777a. No repository exposed a release-population certificate or mandatory pre-train/pre-eval semantic equality gate.

Verified that these systems cover portable workloads, artifact lineage, metadata, schemas, quality assertions, content digests, and custom attestations. They can host pieces of the candidate but do not standardize the cooperative-perception canonical population or require E4.

Verified scenario replay, explicit ego flags, agent and timestamp indexing, dataset-index generation, split manifests, and loader-derived cohorts. These are the strongest domain-specific partial collisions, but none binds the effective loader population to a signed generator receipt and blocks execution on mismatch.

Checked V2X-Real, TUMTraf-V2X, RCooper, and V2X-Seq release and devkit patterns. They publish static splits or indices and official loaders, but their physical events cannot be regenerated by a public simulator generator, so they are not exact collisions.

Searches for evaluation-population certificates, generator-bound cohort manifests, population lineage, and fail-closed release-index validation returned unrelated lineage uses, generic reproducibility, leakage-free generation, or documentation.

searchLimitations: The cutoff includes very recent July 2026 preprints that may not yet be indexed uniformly; absence of an indexed exact collision is not proof of global absence.
Some cooperative datasets require very large downloads or simulator assets. Public code and manifests were inspected, but full regeneration of every release was not executed.
Private industrial release pipelines, unpublished internal checks, and non-English material not discoverable through the queried indexes are outside the evidence set.

A generic framework plus a short custom population checker may be functionally assembled without a paper naming the resulting artifact as a release-population lineage certificate. This substantially limits system-level novelty even though it is not an identified prior implementation.

verifiedNearestWorks.title: SimBEV2X: A Large-Scale Dataset and Data Generation Tool for Multi-Task Vehicle-to-Everything Cooperative Perception
verifiedCapabilities: Public CARLA-based generator with create, replace, and replay modes.
Configuration specifies train, validation, and test scene counts, entity ranges, and scene-number-derived random seeds.
Generation writes split info JSON files and per-scene configuration and log artifacts.
Official repository includes a Dockerfile and a sample data loader.
The loader exposes ego identity and derives the cooperating cohort from loader settings such as sample mode, entity type, communication range, and elevation constraints.
missingForExactEquivalence: The release does not publish a signed canonical population projection containing every event, ego, cohort, split, and population-changing loader option.
Effective ego and cohort membership can be selected or derived at load time and is not bound to the released split-info files.
No mandatory pre-train or pre-eval command regenerates the canonical population and fails on exact set inequality.
The inspected Dockerfile uses mutable dependencies, including a source dependency from a main branch, rather than pinning every dependency by digest or commit.
The project documents replay discrepancies for some simulator actors, so raw replay alone cannot substitute for a normalized semantic population certificate.

verifiedNearestWorks.title: OPV2V, OpenCOOD, and OpenCDA
verifiedCapabilities: The release is organized by split, scenario, agent, and timestamp and stores simulation protocol metadata.
OpenCOOD builds a scenario database indexed by scenario, agent, and timestamp and marks the ego role explicitly in runtime samples.
OpenCDA provides the scenario generator and data-collection path; OpenCOOD documents log replay that preserves recorded events while permitting new sensors.
missingForExactEquivalence: The released dataset is not accompanied by a pinned generator commit, content-addressed container, and signed population manifest covering all release units.
Replay and loader behavior are not compared against a canonical event-by-ego-by-cohort set before training or evaluation.
The ego-relative sample projection is runtime behavior rather than a release-bound semantic certificate.

verifiedNearestWorks.title: Toward Collaborative Autonomous Driving: Simulation Platform and End-to-End System (V2Xverse)

publication.status: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence 47(8)

verifiedCapabilities: Public CARLA-based collaborative-driving generation and evaluation pipeline.
Generation scripts use configured routes and seeds and produce per-ego data.
An official gen_index.py creates dataset_index.txt, which is consumed by training and testing code.
missingForExactEquivalence: The generated index is not a signed canonical population projection bound to generator commit, container digest, assets, and configuration.
No published verifier regenerates event, ego, and cohort semantics from the pinned generator and compares exact set equality before execution.
Index generation is a pipeline step, not a lineage certificate with fail-closed drift detection.

verifiedNearestWorks.title: RCP-Bench: Benchmarking Robustness for Collaborative Perception Under Diverse Corruptions
verifiedCapabilities: Systematically constructs and audits collaborative-perception benchmark variants under corruption, sensor failure, and temporal misalignment.
missingForExactEquivalence: The audit target is robustness under perturbations, not identity between a released evaluation population and its generating process.
It does not bind event, ego, and cohort membership to generator provenance or provide the E4 gate.

verifiedNearestWorks.title: Kubric: A Scalable Dataset Generator
verifiedCapabilities: Public container-oriented synthetic-data generator with explicit seeds, assets, train-test control, and machine-readable outputs and manifests.
missingForExactEquivalence: It is a general generator and does not define cooperative physical events, ego roles, cohorts, or a release-index equality certificate.
No generic Kubric mechanism blocks downstream evaluation when a release population differs semantically from a declared generator population.

verifiedNearestWorks.title: FAIRly big: A framework for computationally reproducible processing of large-scale data
verifiedCapabilities: DataLad records commands, inputs, outputs, source revisions, and container dependencies in Git history and can rerun recorded computations.
Container images can be treated as versioned input dependencies and output changes can be compared after rerun.
missingForExactEquivalence: Artifacts remain generic files unless a domain-specific projection and checker are authored.
No built-in notion of event, ego role, or cohort membership and no standard population-semantic equality gate.

verifiedNearestWorks.title: DVC pipelines and data versioning
verifiedCapabilities: dvc.yaml and lock files encode reproducible commands, dependencies, parameters, outputs, and content hashes.
Git revisions can pin pipeline definitions and DVC-managed artifacts, and dvc repro can rebuild stale outputs.
missingForExactEquivalence: DVC detects dependency and output changes at artifact level, not semantic inequality of a cooperative evaluation population.
A custom projection, equality checker, certificate predicate, and mandatory entrypoint gate would still be required.

verifiedNearestWorks.title: Recording provenance of workflow runs with RO-Crate
verifiedCapabilities: Workflow Run RO-Crate records prospective and retrospective provenance, code, inputs, outputs, checksums, parameters, and container images in a portable bundle.
missingForExactEquivalence: The crate describes a run but does not define the target-domain canonical population or enforce its equality with a release index before downstream use.

verifiedNearestWorks.title: Croissant and Croissant-RAI
verifiedCapabilities: Machine-readable dataset resources, file hashes, record sets, fields, extraction and transformation descriptions, and ML semantics.
Croissant-RAI documents collection, composition, versioning, processing, traceability, and other lifecycle properties.
missingForExactEquivalence: Metadata can describe a population and its files but does not itself execute a simulator generator, derive the canonical event-ego-cohort set, or require exact equality before training and evaluation.
No standard Croissant field or verifier gives the candidate's cooperative-perception population semantics.

verifiedNearestWorks.title: Croissant Tasks: A Metadata Format for Reproducible Machine Learning Evaluations
verifiedCapabilities: Defines declarative, machine-actionable evaluation-task metadata intended to improve conceptual reproducibility and decouple task specification from implementations.
missingForExactEquivalence: No official implementation repository was located in the searched primary sources.
The task description does not establish a generator-bound, signed canonical release population or E4 semantic set gate.

verifiedNearestWorks.title: TensorFlow Datasets and Hugging Face Datasets builders
verifiedCapabilities: Versioned builders declare configurations and splits and mechanically download, prepare, and generate examples.
Checksums, dataset info, split counts, repository revisions, and transformation fingerprints support reproducibility and cache invalidation.
missingForExactEquivalence: Generic examples and split counts do not define physical-event, ego-role, and cooperating-cohort identity.
Neither system supplies a signed release-to-generator population certificate or requires exact semantic preflight equality.

verifiedNearestWorks.title: DataComp and DataPerf
verifiedCapabilities: DataComp makes selected training populations explicit through sample UID lists drawn from a fixed candidate pool and applies fixed training and evaluation procedures.
DataPerf publishes open benchmark definitions and baselines for data-centric algorithm comparison with reproducibility as a stated goal.
missingForExactEquivalence: They benchmark data selection or curation rather than certify that a released evaluation population equals a simulator generator's event-ego-cohort population.
No generator commit, container digest, canonical semantic projection, and fail-closed release-index comparison are combined.

verifiedNearestWorks.title: ML Metadata and OpenLineage
verifiedCapabilities: MLMD records typed artifacts, executions, events, contexts, parameters, and their lineage graph.
OpenLineage standardizes dataset, job, and run metadata and permits extensible facets.
missingForExactEquivalence: Both record generic lineage supplied by integrations; neither defines or verifies cooperative evaluation-population semantics.
Lineage graph presence does not prove equality between a generated canonical population and the release index.

verifiedNearestWorks.title: MLCube and MedPerf
verifiedCapabilities: MLCube specifies portable tasks, entrypoints, parameters, data configuration, and container execution.
MedPerf packages dataset preparation, model execution, and metrics as separate MLCubes for reproducible federated benchmarking.
missingForExactEquivalence: Portable preparation and evaluation workloads do not by themselves certify semantic identity of the evaluation cohort against a public generator.
No cooperative event-ego-cohort projection or release-index mismatch gate is defined.

verifiedNearestWorks.title: in-toto Attestation Framework, SLSA provenance, and Sigstore
verifiedCapabilities: in-toto binds signed statements to artifact subjects, records materials and products, and supports verifier-run inspections whose nonzero result halts validation.
The attestation predicate can contain arbitrary type-specific metadata, while SLSA provenance identifies build inputs and resolved dependencies.
Sigstore bundles signatures, verification material, and DSSE-wrapped attestations and verifies artifacts by digest.
missingForExactEquivalence: The frameworks intentionally treat target artifacts or custom predicate semantics as project-defined; no maintained predicate defines cooperative physical events, ego roles, and cohorts.

An exact solution can be assembled on this substrate only by adding the candidate's domain projection and verifier. The generic certificate and fail-closed mechanism themselves are therefore not novel.

verifiedNearestWorks.title: Data Contract CLI, Open Data Contract Standard, Great Expectations, and TensorFlow Data Validation
verifiedCapabilities: Data contracts can version schemas, semantics, lineage fields, and executable data-quality rules in CI.
Great Expectations and TFDV can detect schema, distribution, drift, skew, and custom SQL or row-level violations.
missingForExactEquivalence: Official Great Expectations guidance distinguishes schema validation from semantic correctness and requires user-defined assertions for the latter.
No standard contract derives the population from a pinned cooperative simulator generator, binds it to a release, and mandates exact event-ego-cohort equality before training or evaluation.

verifiedNearestWorks.title: Data Cards, Datasheets for Datasets, and Model Cards

publication.status: ACM FAccT 2022 for Data Cards; foundational earlier publications for Datasheets and Model Cards

verifiedCapabilities: Structured documentation covers dataset composition, collection, preprocessing, distribution, maintenance, intended uses, evaluation context, and responsible-AI transparency.
missingForExactEquivalence: These are documentation and reporting mechanisms, not executable regeneration, cryptographic binding, or preflight semantic equality systems.

verifiedNearestWorks.title: CLEAN-EVAL, LatestEval, and benchmark contamination or deduplication audits

publication.status: Findings of NAACL 2024 and AAAI 2024 representative records

verifiedCapabilities: Detects, avoids, or mitigates benchmark contamination, training-test overlap, memorization, or duplicate samples.
missingForExactEquivalence: Leakage identity is a relation between training sources and evaluation examples, not equality between a release index and its generator-defined event-ego-cohort population.
No generator provenance certificate or E4 population gate is provided.

verifiedNearestWorks.title: Forensic Reproducibility Audit of a Radiology VLM Benchmark: From Intended Protocol to Released Artifact
verifiedCapabilities: Audits divergence between intended benchmark protocol and released artifacts, including cohort reconstruction and lost split membership.
Calls for machine-verifiable controls spanning cohort, rendering, prompts, model calls, annotations, keyed analysis, and derived artifacts.
missingForExactEquivalence: The searched primary record did not expose an official generator, pinned container, signed population manifest, or executable pre-evaluation set-equality gate.
It is a retrospective cross-domain audit rather than the complete release-time certificate.

partialCollisions.collision: These works already publish generators or replay paths, split or dataset indices, explicit ego or agent structures, and training/evaluation loaders. They remove novelty from the ideas of public generation, explicit ego indexing, and generator-to-index pipelines considered separately.
partialCollisions.notExactBecause: They do not publish a cryptographically bound canonical event-ego-cohort population and do not fail closed before training or evaluation when regenerated semantics differ.

partialCollisions.collision: Public generators, dataset builders, DVC, DataLad, RO-Crate, MLMD, OpenLineage, MLCube, and MedPerf already cover most mechanical plumbing: versioned code, containers, inputs, parameters, commands, outputs, hashes, reruns, and lineage graphs.
partialCollisions.notExactBecause: Their semantic unit is a generic artifact, record, dataset, task, or workflow; the event-ego-cohort population and exact release equality rule remain domain-defined.

partialCollisions.collision: Croissant, Croissant-RAI, Croissant Tasks, data contracts, data-quality suites, datasheets, data cards, and model cards already cover machine-readable structure, lifecycle metadata, intended semantics, and extensible quality assertions.
partialCollisions.notExactBecause: Description or representability is not proof that the released evaluation population was generated by the declared process, and these systems do not standardize the target projection or E4.

partialCollisions.collision: in-toto, SLSA, and Sigstore already provide signed subject binding, materials and products, provenance predicates, digest verification, and verifier-time inspections that can halt on a failed custom command.
partialCollisions.notExactBecause: They do not supply the cooperative-perception population predicate or projection. This is a partial rather than exact collision, but it destroys novelty for a generic claim to inventing a certificate or fail-closed attestation mechanism.

partialCollisions.collision: Prior audits already test benchmark robustness, released-artifact divergence, cohort reconstruction, duplication, and contamination and have articulated machine-verifiable controls.
partialCollisions.notExactBecause: They do not combine public generator replay, pinned environment, canonical cooperative population semantics, signed release binding, and mandatory preflight equality.

partialCollisions.collision: DataComp demonstrates that a benchmark population can be made operational through explicit stable sample identifiers and a fixed downstream protocol.
partialCollisions.notExactBecause: The population is selected from a candidate pool rather than regenerated as physical events with ego and cohort roles, and no generator-bound certificate is checked.

remainingNarrowGap.statement: As of the cutoff, the only uncollided unit found is a cooperative-perception-specific executable contract that derives a canonical event-by-ego-by-cohort evaluation population from a pinned public generator and separately from the released index, cryptographically binds both derivations and all population-changing configuration, and blocks every training and evaluation entrypoint unless exact semantic set equality holds.
requiredTechnicalContent: A normative schema for physical_event_id, temporal extent, ego identity and role, cohort membership, split, sensor or infrastructure role, and population-changing loader filters.
Two independent projectors: one from generator inputs and execution receipt, and one from the release index and actual loader semantics.
Canonicalization rules for ordering, aliases, replay nondeterminism, entity births and deaths, missing frames, and dynamic communication-range cohorts.
Pinned generator source commit, simulator and map or asset identities, content-addressed container digest, parameters, random seeds, and declared nondeterminism policy.
A signed or content-addressed certificate whose subject includes the release artifacts and whose predicate includes both canonical population digests and generation provenance.
A verifier installed as an unavoidable precondition of all official train and eval entrypoints, with nonzero exit on any semantic difference or unbound option.

Demonstration on at least one released cooperative benchmark where the checker detects a real or intentionally injected index-versus-generator population drift that byte hashes, schemas, and leakage audits miss.
remainingNarrowGap.whyNarrow: The generator, container, manifest, versioning, signature, workflow provenance, and fail-closed inspection mechanisms already exist in adjacent tools. Novelty cannot rest on composing those generic components; it must rest on the domain ontology, canonical projection, mandatory integration, and demonstrated detection of population-semantic drift.

noveltyFailureConditions.condition: A pre-cutoff public implementation is found that satisfies E1-E4, even under another name or in another application domain.
noveltyFailureConditions.effect: Exact functional collision; the system claim fails.

noveltyFailureConditions.condition: The proposed certificate only hashes release files, index bytes, DVC outputs, container images, or manifests without deriving population semantics.
noveltyFailureConditions.effect: Collapsed into generic artifact lineage and attestation represented by W06-W08, W13, and W15.

noveltyFailureConditions.condition: Event, ego, and cohort fields are only documented in Croissant, a data contract, a datasheet, or prose and are not recomputed from both generator and release.
noveltyFailureConditions.effect: Collapsed into schema and metadata work represented by W09, W10, W16, and W17.

noveltyFailureConditions.condition: The method is an in-toto, SLSA, Sigstore, RO-Crate, DVC, or DataLad wrapper with a project-specific check but contributes no normative cooperative population schema, canonicalization, or evidence of a previously invisible drift.
noveltyFailureConditions.effect: The composition may be useful engineering but lacks a distinct research contribution over the verified substrate.

noveltyFailureConditions.condition: The generator commit or container is mutable, simulator assets or maps are unpinned, seeds or population filters are omitted, or effective loader options can change ego or cohort membership outside the certificate.
noveltyFailureConditions.effect: E2 or E3 fails; the certificate cannot establish the claimed lineage.

noveltyFailureConditions.condition: Validation compares only counts, file names, aggregate distributions, schema, or sample checks rather than exact canonical population equality.
noveltyFailureConditions.effect: E4 fails and semantic substitutions, omissions, or role changes can pass.

noveltyFailureConditions.condition: The check is optional, runs after training or evaluation, logs a warning, or can be bypassed by an official entrypoint.
noveltyFailureConditions.effect: The claimed pre-execution fail-closed property is absent.

noveltyFailureConditions.condition: The released population cannot be derived independently from actual release artifacts and loader semantics, so the verifier merely trusts the generator-produced manifest on both sides.
noveltyFailureConditions.effect: The equality check is circular and cannot detect release-index drift.

noveltyFailureConditions.condition: Replay nondeterminism is ignored or raw sensor-byte equality is required where the simulator cannot reproduce bytes, without a justified canonical semantic projection.
noveltyFailureConditions.effect: The certificate either produces false assurance or is unusable; the claimed semantic guarantee is not established.

noveltyFailureConditions.condition: The empirical study only detects training-test leakage, duplicate frames, corruptions, or distribution shift.
noveltyFailureConditions.effect: Collapsed into leakage and robustness audits represented by W04 and W18 rather than the target population-lineage problem.

noveltyFailureConditions.condition: A release update can change an index, loader, generator, configuration, or population projection without invalidating and reissuing the certificate.
noveltyFailureConditions.effect: The certificate is not release-bound and E3 fails.

noveltyFailureConditions.condition: The contribution is claimed broadly as the first reproducible benchmark, first dataset manifest, first provenance certificate, first generator-to-index pipeline, or first fail-closed verification framework.
noveltyFailureConditions.effect: The claim is directly contradicted by multiple verified partial collisions even though no E1-E4 package was found.

potentiallyDefensibleOnlyIfImplemented: A first date-bounded implementation of generator-bound release-population semantic equality specifically for cooperative perception, not a first provenance or reproducibility certificate in general.
A normative canonical population model that treats physical event, ego role, and cooperating cohort as the evaluation unit and binds all loader-dependent population choices.
An independent two-sided derivation and mandatory preflight verifier that detects release-index drift before any official training or evaluation path.
Empirical evidence that this semantic check catches defects missed by file hashes, generic lineage, schema validation, and leakage or corruption audits.
notDefensible: First public or reproducible cooperative-perception simulator or dataset generator.
First cooperative benchmark with scenarios, agents, ego identities, splits, replay, or a generated dataset index.
First versioned data pipeline, containerized evaluation workload, workflow provenance record, signed manifest, or supply-chain attestation.
First machine-readable dataset metadata, data contract, dataset card, datasheet, model card, or evaluation-task schema.
First benchmark leakage, corruption, robustness, release-artifact, or cohort audit.
First use of custom assertions or verifier-time commands to fail a pipeline.
Any guarantee of raw byte-for-byte simulator replay unless every source of nondeterminism and every asset is actually pinned and demonstrated.
claimBoundary.requiredWordingConstraint: Any novelty statement must name the event-ego-cohort canonical projection, two-sided release-versus-generator derivation, cryptographic release binding, and unavoidable pre-execution equality gate. Omitting any of these makes the statement overbroad relative to verified prior work.

verdict.finding: No verified paper, proceedings artifact, official tool, or cooperative-perception repository found by the cutoff implements all E1-E4 as one released system. However, the broad certificate concept is heavily preempted: domain benchmarks already provide generators, replay, ego and agent indices, and generated dataset indices, while generic tools already provide reproducible execution, content lineage, signed attestations, custom predicates, and fail-closed inspections.
verdict.noveltyPosition: The candidate has no defensible novelty as a generic benchmark provenance, manifest, reproducibility, or certification system. A residual claim exists only for the cooperative-perception-specific canonical population semantics and their mandatory two-sided preflight equality enforcement, backed by a concrete released artifact and a demonstrated mismatch that existing checks miss.
verdict.collisionHandling: SimBEV2X, OPV2V/OpenCOOD/OpenCDA, V2Xverse, in-toto, DataLad, Croissant, and data-contract tooling must be treated as substantive partial collisions, not background conveniences. If subsequent inspection reveals that any one of these, or another pre-cutoff work, already binds and enforces the same canonical event-ego-cohort population, it must move to exactCollisions and the remaining system claim fails.
